findings.location: Two-factor setup, verification code, first message
findings.evidence: "Check the message again and enter all six."
findings.violation: The message instructs the user to check again without explicitly stating that the verification code is incomplete.
findings.fix: Rewrite as "Your verification code must be exactly 6 digits."

findings.location: Two-factor setup, verification code, first message
findings.evidence: Verification codes are 6 digits long, and this one has 5. Check the message again and enter all six.
findings.violation: The message leads with technical explanation (digit count comparison) before the actionable error, delaying comprehension.

findings.location: Two-factor setup, verification code, second message
findings.evidence: "This verification code expired 10 minutes after it was sent, which stops an intercepted code from being reused later."
findings.violation: The message specifies the expiration window but provides no reference point for the current time, making it impossible for users to evaluate urgency.
findings.fix: Add the time sent or absolute expiration time: "This code expired 10 minutes after it was sent at 2:45 PM."

findings.evidence: "This promo code applies to annual plans, and the selected plan is monthly."
findings.violation: The passive phrasing "the selected plan is monthly" does not clearly name which specific plan or tier the user has selected.
findings.fix: Change to "This promo code works with annual plans only. You selected a monthly plan."

findings.evidence: "Signal: bold text set larger than the field label, icon" (appears in all four message blocks)
findings.violation: All four messages use identical visual treatment despite representing different error types and urgencies, reducing visual hierarchy.
findings.fix: Differentiate signals by severity: use larger bold text and warning icon for time-sensitive errors, standard bold for configuration errors.

findings.evidence: "Fires: on-blur" appears for first and third messages; "Fires: on-submit" appears for second and fourth messages
findings.violation: The timing pattern is inconsistent, appearing arbitrary without explanation of why validation timing differs.
findings.fix: Document the rationale or standardize to a consistent trigger point.
